title: Node Fleet Registry & Health Signals — Service Discovery Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This note captures an implementation sketch for a Node Fleet Registry and health signal model that will serve Redwood's multi-region service discovery and routing policies (hosted, dedicated, private). It focuses on: node labeling and canonical GPU typing, health signal set and evaluation rules, the control-plane API for inventory queries, and implications for routing decisions (latency/cost/availability).

Goals:
- Provide a compact, searchable registry of nodes (physical and VM) across regions and zones.
- Standardize node labels and GPU type taxonomy to enable policy-driven routing and automated fallbacks.
- Define a health signal set and scoring function usable by the control plane and by local proxies.
- Keep registry read paths low-latency and resilient to partial control plane outages.

Design principles and constraints:
- Read-mostly: routers and schedulers will query inventory frequently; favor caching and lightweight query APIs.
- Compact labels: avoid long free-form tags — prefer a small set of typed labels for indexing.
- GPU-first semantics: many routing decisions are GPU-aware (quantize profile compatibility, memory, compute class).
- Multi-region consistency: prefer eventual consistency but provide strong-affinity pins when customer requires it.
- Health score deterministic: scoring must be idempotent and explainable for incident analysis.

Canonical node model (flat key set for registry rows):
- node_id: string (UUID)
- hostname: string
- region: string (e.g., us-west1)
- zone: string (e.g., us-west1-b)
- pool: string (eg. dedicated-pool-12)
- role: string (inference-worker | control-plane | infra)
- gpu_family: string (A100-40GB | A100-80GB | H100-80GB | T4)
- gpu_count: string ("1", "4", "8")
- gpu_mem_gb: string ("40", "80")
- cpu_vcpu: string ("32")
- host_memory_gb: string ("512")
- kernel_version: string
- driver_version: string
- nvml_hash: string (for exact driver/KV match)
- last_seen: string (RFC3339)
- health_state: string (healthy | degraded | unhealthy)
- health_score: string (0-100)
- tags: [list of short strings]
- capabilities: [list of short strings] (e.g., fp16, int8, kv-cache-local)

Notes on fields: all numeric values are stored as strings in the registry row to keep schema simple across storage backends and to match the flattened JSON format used by the control-plane. gpu_family is a canonical enum that maps to a set of compatibility profiles (see compatibility table below).

GPU taxonomy and compatibility profiles (examples):
- A100-40GB => profile: a100-40, supports: fp16, bf16, int8 (quantization depends on runtime kernels)
- A100-80GB => profile: a100-80, supports: same as a100-40 but larger KV cache
- H100-80GB => profile: h100-80, supports: fp8, fp16, bf16, int8 (preferred for large context/low latency)
- T4 => profile: t4, supports: fp16 (lower throughput)

These profiles are referenced by routing policy rules (e.g., prefer h100 for latency-sensitive models, allow a100 for most general workloads).

Health signals and scoring:
We collect three signal classes: local kernel signals, workload telemetry, and control-plane heartbeats. Each node emits a minimal health envelope every 15s; the control-plane ingests and computes a rolling health score on these signals.

Signal examples (minimal set):
- heartbeat_ts: last agent heartbeat (RFC3339)
- cpu_load_1m: string (float)
- cpu_util_pct: string (0-100)
- gpu_power_draw: string (watts)
- gpu_util_pct: string (0-100)
- gpu_mem_used_gb: string
- gpu_temp_c: string
- nvlink_errors: string (count)
- kernel_oops_recent: string (bool)
- pod_evictions_5m: string (count)
- network_rtt_ms: string (p50)
- disk_io_wait_pct: string

Scoring function (control-plane):
- base = 100
- subtract 10 if heartbeat_ts older than 45s
- subtract 20 if gpu_util_pct > 98 and gpu_mem_used_gb > (gpu_mem_gb - 2)
- subtract 30 if kernel_oops_recent == true or nvlink_errors > 0
- subtract 15 if pod_evictions_5m > 0
- clamp to [0, 100] and set health_state based on thresholds (>=90 healthy, 60-89 degraded, <60 unhealthy)

Routing implications and control-plane API contract:
- Inventory query API: GET /v1/inventory?region=us-west1&gpu_family=h100-80&min_health=80&pool=dedicated-*
  - returns a paginated list of node rows (flat JSON list).
- Agent cache hints: responses include cache_ttl_seconds and a cursor token for delta pulls. Routers should cache for TTL and subscribe to push updates for deviations.
- Prefetch rules: control-plane will proactively push topology deltas to edge routers when health_score delta > 20 for nodes in their affinity set.
- Fallback rules: if preferred profile not available within latency SLO, the router can select next-compatible profile but must set metadata tags on the request indicating fallback reason (for billing/metrics).

Control-plane storage and sharding model (notes):
- Region-sharded keyspace: primary copy per region with global index of node_id -> home-region. This allows local reads with eventual cross-region consistency for global queries.
- Hot nodes (high-change) kept in an in-memory cache (redis or etcd tier) for sub-100ms reads. Cold nodes in analytic store (Bigtable/Spanner equivalent).
- Delta stream exposed via a lightweight websocket/HTTP2 stream endpoint for subscribers (routers, autoscalers).

Agent design (node-side):
- Single binary plugin that collects signals and reports compressed protobuf envelope every 15s.
- Minimal local evaluation: detect immediate kernel oops, disable GPU acceptance locally and flag a forced-degraded state until human/operator clears.
- Secure authentication to control-plane using per-node short-lived certs issued by the control-plane CA.

Operational playbooks (short):
- Node enters unhealthy: control plane moves node to cordon state and marks pool capacity lower. Routers receive delta and route away. Alert to oncall with node context + recent traces.
- Flapping nodes: if health_score oscillates more than 30 points in 10m, auto-cordon and open ticket (JIRA) with prefilled diagnostics.
- Driver upgrades: nodes that receive driver changes must report driver_version and nvml_hash; control-plane will mark as transitional and route only test traffic unless explicitly allowed.

Migration considerations from current inventory:
- Provide a compatibility shim that maps existing free-form GPU labels into canonical gpu_family values; run a two-week shadow sync where both systems serve reads and compare routing decisions and metrics.
- Gradually switch critical services to read new API in canary mode, then flip region-by-region.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How aggressive should push notifications be to edge routers? Too frequent pushes increase control-plane load; too infrequent increases stale routing decisions. Proposal: delta threshold of health_score >= 20 or node addition/removal.
- Do we compute health_score centrally or allow router-local adjustments? Central compute ensures consistency; router-local adjust allows site-tailored policies (e.g., prefer cheaper nodes at cost of some latency). Proposal: central score + optional local modifiers applied at router with audit trail.
- Storage backend choices: Spanner-like global consistency vs region-local low-latency store with global index. Current recommendation: region-local primary with background global index replication.

Next actions / TODOs:
- Draft API OpenAPI spec for inventory endpoints (GET inventory, GET node/{id}, POST agent/envelope) — owner: Aisha (ETA 2026-03-20).
- Implement proto for agent envelope and small reference agent for Linux nodes — owner: Marcus (ETA 2026-04-03).
- Run migration shadow sync and build comparison dashboard — owner: Sofia (ETA 2026-04-17).
